title: OUGH and AUGH Rebels
kidRule: In O-U-G-H and A-U-G-H words, the G and H never make their usual sounds. Mostly they stay quiet, like in BOUGHT, and sometimes they say 'f', like in LAUGH. These words are rebels, so learn them with your eyes!
hint: This word has a sneaky four-letter team, and two of its letters do not make their usual sounds. Picture the word in your mind. What does the team look like?
reminder: This word uses a four-letter team: O-U-G-H or A-U-G-H. If one did not work, try the other one!

check.question: Why can't we hear a G sound in BOUGHT?
check.correctAnswer: Because G and H are part of the O-U-G-H team, and they stay quiet here!
distractors: Because G is always quiet in the middle of a word
Because the letter T tells every letter before it to hush

words.sent: I bought a kite with my birthday money.
words.story: In 1867 the United States bought Alaska from Russia for about two cents an acre!
words.card: '*Ugh*, I *bought* a hat made of spaghetti by mistake!'

words.def: To make happy sounds when something is funny.
words.story: Rats laugh when they are tickled! Their giggles are too high for our ears, so scientists use special microphones to hear them.
words.card: '*La*, *la*, *la*,' sang the hyena, and then she began to *laugh*!

words.def: A word that means 'but' or 'even if'.
words.sent: The soup was hot, though it tasted great.
words.story: Long ago, people really did say the GH in this word, with a scratchy sound made in the throat. The sound faded away, but the letters stayed!
words.card: The mouse built a *hou*se of cheese, *though* he kept eating the walls!

words.sent: We have enough apples for everyone.
words.story: A blue whale can eat about four tons of tiny krill in one day. That is enough food to weigh as much as an elephant!
words.card: '*No*, *no*, that is *enough* ketchup for one goldfish!'

words.def: A girl or woman who is someone's child.
words.sent: The queen read a story to her daughter.
words.story: Every worker bee in a hive is a daughter of the queen bee, and the daughters do all the work!
words.card: The ot*ter*'s *daughter* juggles clams for her breakfast!

words.def: To push air out of your throat with a sudden, noisy burst.
words.sent: Cover your mouth when you cough.
words.story: When you cough, the air can rush out of your mouth at up to about 50 miles an hour!
words.card: The *cou*ch gave a dusty *cough* when the hippo sat down!

words.def: Strong and hard to break or hurt.
words.sent: The tough old boots lasted for years.
words.story: Tiny water bears are some of the toughest creatures on Earth. They can survive being frozen, boiled, and even sent into outer space!
words.card: The *tou*can thinks he is *tough* because he can crack a peanut!

words.def: Carried or took something with you to a place.
words.sent: She brought her teddy bear to the picnic.
words.story: The Apollo astronauts brought 842 pounds of Moon rocks back to Earth!
words.card: The *rough* old pirate *brought* his teddy bear to the sleepover!

words.def: Behaving badly or not doing what you are told.
words.sent: The naughty puppy chewed my sock.
words.story: Kea parrots in New Zealand are famously naughty. They love to pull the rubber strips off parked cars!
words.card: '*Ugh*!' said Mom when the *naughty* puppy hid her slippers in the pond!

words.def: A word that means 'in spite of the fact that'.
words.sent: Although it was raining, we played outside.
words.story: This word began as the two words 'all though'. They squished together, and one L got lost along the way!
words.card: *Al* the alligator won the race, *although* he ran it backwards!
